## Time and location quality

Timestamp diagnostics are screening rules, not proof that times are accurate.
Darkness analysis excludes force-months that fail or lack a reliable-time flag.

{{timestamps}}

Coordinates are anonymised snap points. Boundary sensitivity measures proximity
to a geography edge; it does not measure or correct true location error.
The boundary-sensitive share uses assigned events with measured distances.
Missing-coordinate and unassigned shares use all supplied events.

{{geography}}

## Estimates

Each supplied analysis retains its own scope, exposures and exclusions. Rates
use submitted population-time. Sampling intervals condition on the model and
denominator. They do not quantify uncertainty about unobserved ethnicity,
population movement, Census measurement or incomplete submissions.

{{estimates}}

## Assumptions

Resident Census population is an exposure choice. It may differ from the people
present or exposed to police activity. Missing-ethnicity allocations are stated
scenarios. Their ranges are not confidence intervals and are not combined with
sampling uncertainty. Spatial smoothing stabilises under its model assumptions;
inspect unsmoothed data, local changes and convergence diagnostics.

{{assumptions}}

## Limitations

Repeated events, deployment, activity, selection and measurement can affect
comparisons. Hit rates condition on being searched and do not by themselves
establish discrimination. Darkness associations require assumptions about
visibility and comparable activity and deployment. The method originated for
vehicle stops; its transfer to pedestrian searches requires justification.
Neither an undefined result nor a wide interval establishes absence of disparity.

{{limitations}}
